function: Autoencoder compresses the passive BD-RIS configuration to cut control rate and enables its optimization in the latent space; SDP/PGA with randomization gives the target configurations (pp. 1, 6-8).
system: Narrowband mmWave downlink: BS ULA with 6 antennas, user ULA with 2 antennas, passive reflecting BD-RIS with group-, fully-connected or diagonal architecture; blocked direct link (pp. 3, 9).
method: Autoencoder (single linear layer, or deep with ReLU) trained unsupervised on SDP-based BD-RIS configurations with MSE or negative-rate loss; decoder output normalized for passivity (pp. 6-7, 11-12).
data_channel: Simulated geometric mmWave channels: 2 paths, uniform random angles, complex Gaussian path gains, ULA response; 8·10^4 training samples, 10^4 validation and 10^4 test (pp. 9, 11).
test_conditions: Trained and tested on the same simulated channel distribution, N = 8, SNR 10 dB, held-out test samples; rate evaluated after quantization at various control rates (pp. 11, 14).
baselines: Classical, non-learned: FC-NDE, FC-UC (optimal fully-connected), D-NDE, D-LC (diagonal); no earlier learned method; BAE versus DON autoencoder variants (pp. 10-12).
metrics: Average achievable rate of the cascade channel; rate loss of AE output versus RCO; configuration MSE; complexity versus N; rate versus control bits (pp. 10-14).
complexity: Orders: SDP O((N Nbar)^6), O(c^6) in latent space; PGA O(T N c^2); randomization O(P (N Nbar)^3); Fig. 14 plots total complexity versus N (pp. 6, 8-9, 13).
q1_support: p. 9: "path gains are zero-mean and unitary variance independent complex Gaussian variables". Custom two-path geometric model with uniform random angles; no 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "We split the dataset into 8 · 104 samples for training, 104 for both validation and testing". Held-out part of the same simulated data; a separate autoencoder is trained per N, c and loss, and training is to be repeated when conditions change (p. 7).
q3_support: p. 10: "We consider the following solutions for comparison". The four solutions (FC-NDE, FC-UC, D-NDE, D-LC) are non-learned; BAE and DON are variants of the proposed autoencoder, and the learned compressors of refs [19], [20] are cited but not simulated.
q4_support: p. 6: "The computational complexity of solving the SDP scales as O((N N )6 )". Orders for PGA, randomization and the latent-space design are on pp. 6, 8-9, and Fig. 14 on p. 13 plots the overall complexity.
q5_support: p. 9: "Since channels in the mmWave band have only a few relevant paths, we use a geometric model to describe them". Self-generated data; no code or dataset link or DOI appears in the paper.
notes: Area 3: the learned part is the autoencoder that compresses and maps the BD-RIS configuration (pp. 6-8); SDP, PGA and randomization are non-learned. The linear autoencoder used for latent-space design is equivalent to PCA (p. 8). q2: separate autoencoders per N, c and loss, tested on held-out samples of the same distribution; test-time quantization (p. 14) is not a new scenario. q3: all compared solutions are non-learned; autoencoder variants are not earlier methods. q4: complexity orders are for the proposed design, no runtime. q5: no code or data statement.
